summary: pay-methods-kmf exfiltrates host and npm registry metadata to hardcoded IP on require
details: pay-methods-kmf@100.100.100 ships a stub index.js (module.exports = {}) and a Linux x64 native addon at prebuilds/linux-x64/addon.node that is loaded on require and from postinstall.js. The addon's napi_register_module_v1 entrypoint reads HOSTNAME, npm_package_name, and npm_config_registry via getenv, forks, opens a raw socket to 64.181.165.115, and issues 'POST /dc HTTP/1.0' with a url-encoded body of the form h=<hostname>&p=<package name>&u=<user>&r=<registry URL>. The implausibly high synthetic version number (100.100.100), empty JS surface, and payload shape (reporting the configured npm registry alongside the package name and host) are characteristic of a dependency-confusion exfiltration beacon that fires automatically when the package is installed or required.
